B: Hiya. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah, hello. Tomasz.
B: Rob. Last one, this, isn't it?
A: Yeah. Neil said last time was last one, but no.
B: Ha. I had Neil earlier. He's sound. I sorted his bird out for him.
A: The bird on feeder? He told me also. Dunnock, yeah?
B: That's it. Word travels. So what do you do?
A: Kitchen fitter. Carpenter, in Basingstoke. And you are the student, the birds.
B: Yeah, ecology. Everyone's got me sussed before I open my mouth today.
A: Is the binoculars in picture. Easy.
B: Fair. Did you have a good chat with Neil, then?
A: Yeah. He wants to fix his bike, it's in the shed for twenty years maybe. I told him, chain, brake pads, is easy.
B: Do you do bikes as well?
A: In my garage, yeah. Old ones, from the tip, from Facebook. For my son and his friends. One last month only needed new brakes. People throw away good bikes, is crazy.
B: I could do with you, honestly. I cycle to the station every day and my back brake's been squealing for about a month. I just sort of ignore it.
A: Squealing is usually dirty, or pads are worn. You clean the rim, with, er, little bit of alcohol, the spray. And check the pads. If they're flat and shiny, you sand them a bit or new ones, maybe five pounds.
B: Five quid. Right. I've been dreading taking it in, money's a bit tight at the minute.
A: No, don't take it in. Is ten minutes. YouTube.
B: I'll do it this weekend. Hannah'll be shocked.
A: Ha. My wife also, when I finish something. I have garden bench, one year nearly done.
B: Gemma told me about the bench. Well, no, she told me about her husband's shed. Sounds like the same problem.
A: Yeah, she said. Half roof, three legs. Same club.
B: What do you do outside of work, then, apart from bikes?
A: Fishing. Carp, at a lake near Alton. Sometimes I stay overnight.
B: Oh, nice. You must see loads at night. Owls, bats over the water?
A: Yeah, the bats, every night, very low on the water. I don't know what kind.
B: Probably Daubenton's, if they're skimming right on the surface. They're basically trawling for insects. If you had a detector you'd hear them clicking away.
A: Ah. I just watch them. Is nice, it's quiet, nobody there, only bats.
B: That's sort of my favourite bit of the surveys as well. Standing in a field at midnight. Nobody asks you anything.
A: Yeah. And in the morning, the mist on the lake, and the coffee from flask. Best coffee.
B: Better than the garage stuff.
A: Much better. Garage coffee is, er, I drink it because I have to.
B: Ha. Same with the uni canteen. Is it far, the lake? I'd quite like to
